versions.name: In step with the print
versions.summary: The 3D twin runs along the print's own G-code and keeps in step with the printer, projects from any slicer bring their colours onto the four heads, and notifications count repeats and wait for you.

highlights.title: In step with the print
highlights.text: While a print runs, the nozzle follows the file's own G-code and is checked against the printer about four times a second. Walls appear where and when they are laid. The line under the twin says whether it is in step.

highlights.title: Colours on four heads
highlights.text: Bring a project from MakerWorld, Printables, Bambu Studio, Creality Print, PrusaSlicer or another slicer. Open it to see which head prints each colour; five or more colours are grouped by likeness, and you can change any of them.

highlights.title: From your slicer
highlights.text: Look on this computer finds recent projects in eight slicers, so you can keep your slicer and use Deja Vu1 beside it.

highlights.title: Calmer notifications
highlights.text: A repeated message counts up instead of stacking, a long one stays longer, and the line along the bottom shows the time left. Point at a message to hold it.

changes: The 3D twin follows the running print's own G-code: each reading of the printer's live position and the byte it has read fixes the moment in the file, and between readings the nozzle runs along the path at the printer's own pace. Walls appear where and when they are laid; a tool change or park shows the live position. Tested against a printer simulated from the sample file: within 0.016 s between readings.

Files shows Colours on the U1's heads for a multi-colour project: which filaments the model uses, a suggested head for each (alike colours share, unused ones are left out, or the closest loaded head), and Save a copy with these heads. The converter fits five or more colours by itself.

The converter takes projects from Creality Print, QIDI Studio, Flashforge Orca, other Orca forks and PrusaSlicer, besides MakerWorld, NexPrint and OrcaSlicer. Pick up where you left off finds recent projects in eight slicers, and an Orca preset profile can set a filament per head.
Converting and fitting colours sit under the slice bar in the slicing workspace.

Notifications count repeats, stay longer for long messages, show the time left, wait while the tab is hidden and can be flicked away on a phone. Open the same here? moves into the orb after nine seconds.
Large replies are sent compressed (a print preview from 842 KB to 271 KB), file names wrap at underscores and dots, and Cura's outer walls and skins are drawn in the twin.

versions.name: One thing at a time
versions.summary: Busy screens show one part at a time, slicing sets itself up in five steps with a slicer finder, other Klipper printers can join, and search goes where it says.

highlights.title: One part at a time
highlights.text: Each busy screen opens on one part. These buttons show the others, and Everything shows the whole page. Your choice is remembered.

highlights.title: Get ready to slice
highlights.text: Five steps, once. Find it for me looks for Snapmaker Orca or OrcaSlicer on this computer, so you never type a path. The next step always has the only button.

highlights.title: Other Klipper printers
highlights.text: Any printer that runs Klipper with Moonraker can join. Deja Vu1 reads its size and heads from the printer and checks every file against them.

highlights.title: Search that lands
highlights.text: Type what you want, like slicer or telemetry, and press Enter. It opens the right screen and the right part. On a phone, search is under More.

changes: Overview, Printers, Files, Care and Settings open on one part of the screen, with buttons for the other parts and Everything for the full page. Settings is no longer one long scroll. Search, tours and links open the part that holds what they point at.

Files → Slicing starts with Get ready to slice: turn on, find the slicer, check it, pick presets, add a model. Find it for me lists Snapmaker Orca and OrcaSlicer programs in the usual folders; Use this saves and checks one. With none found, it links both free slicers.
When Slice is greyed out on a plate, it says why and links the set-up. "Auto-print" now reads "Slicing" everywhere.

Printers that run Klipper with Moonraker connect as an untested type. Their size, heads, kinematics and nozzle come from the printer's own report, and the pre-flight and Confirm Print check files against them. A printer that doesn't report its size gets a warning, never a guess.
The search box's Go to results open their card again: a title's help button had stopped most of them matching.
On Overview, the phone card sits under Print health, and a row left with one card uses the full width.
Two unused launch-film copies are gone: each update download is 56 MB instead of 74 MB.

highlights.title: What changed
highlights.text: Every version is listed here, newest first. Open What changed for the full list.

versions.name: Your phone, from anywhere
versions.summary: Open Deja Vu1 on your phone on any network, privately, with one button and a code to scan. The notification orb is now a single glass sphere that changes colour.

highlights.title: Away from home
highlights.text: With Tailscale on this computer and your phone, one button gives Deja Vu1 a private address. Scan the code and your phone opens it on mobile data or any Wi-Fi.

highlights.title: A glass orb
highlights.text: Notifications live in one translucent sphere. It glows green, amber or red with a new message, and turns blue again once you've read them.

changes: Settings → Away from home finds Tailscale on this computer, turns on private sharing (Tailscale Serve, never Funnel) with one button, walks through switching on HTTPS once, and shows a code for the phone. Only this computer can switch it on or off.
The shared address is https, so Chrome on the phone installs Deja Vu1 directly.
The remote guide covers the Extended Firmware's own Tailscale option for reaching the printer itself.
The notification orb has no centre dot: the whole sphere takes the message's colour and stays see-through.

versions.name: Connections you can count on
versions.summary: Printers with a password, the Extended Firmware's camera and printer firmware 2.0.0 now connect the way their own code expects. The phone layout is simpler, Android phones can install the app, and the background dots are one colour you choose.

highlights.title: Sign in to your printer
highlights.text: Type just the printer's numbers. If its web page asks for a login, enter that username and password once: the app reads the printer's key and never keeps the password.

highlights.title: Find my printer's camera
highlights.text: One press asks the printer which camera it has, checks that a picture really arrives and saves the address. Works with the Extended Firmware's camera.

highlights.title: One dot colour
highlights.text: Every background dot is now one colour. Pick it under Dot colour, or choose any colour at all.

highlights.title: A simpler phone
highlights.text: Open Deja Vu1 on your phone: search, help, camera and the rarer screens live under More, and More → Install app puts it on the home screen.

changes: Printers whose web page asks for a login (the Extended Firmware's Web Authentication) connect with that username and password, used once to read the printer's API key. The password is never saved.
Printer addresses can be typed as just the numbers (192.168.1.50); the app adds http:// and Moonraker's port.

Camera: the camera Moonraker lists (the Extended Firmware's /webcam/snapshot.jpg) is used first, then Snapmaker's own monitor, now sent with the req_id it expects and with a failed reply shown as a failure.
Settings → Camera → Find my printer's camera fills in and checks the live feed address.
Printer firmware 2.0.0: a file whose name contains #, * or ; is refused before sending, in words, because the U1 cannot start it.
Phone: a shorter first screen, a one-row print bar, and a More sheet with search, every other screen, Camera, help and Install app. Computer-only cards stay on the computer.
Android: Install app explains the one Chrome setting a home-network address needs, with copy buttons, and installs in one tap once Chrome allows it.
Background: all dots are one colour (no more orange and black band while printing), chosen under Settings → Appearance → Dot colour.
The app and product page drop the testing-status notes; the link preview image was redrawn.

versions.name: Updates that install every time
versions.summary: The Install button works again, every merge on GitHub now becomes a release, and you can update with one pasted command. Settings can restart, repair or stop this copy, your phone connects by QR code, and every card explains itself.

highlights.title: Install works
highlights.text: 0.8.0's Install button crashed before it downloaded anything. Now Check for updates, then Install, and Deja Vu1 restarts into the new version.

highlights.title: A release with every merge
highlights.text: Every change merged on GitHub becomes a new numbered version, listed here. Updates arrive small and often.

highlights.title: Look after this copy
highlights.text: Restart the dashboard, put the published app files back, make a safety copy, or stop Deja Vu1. Your data stays put.

highlights.title: Update with a command
highlights.text: Another way in: one paste for Windows or Mac and Linux stops Deja Vu1, installs the newest release and starts it again.

highlights.title: Your phone, by QR code
highlights.text: Connect your phone shows a code. Point the phone's camera at it and the dashboard opens and pairs by itself.

changes: Fixed: 0.8.0's Install button crashed in its slicing check before downloading anything. A failing check no longer blocks the update that fixes it.
Every merge to main publishes a numbered release by itself; automatic checks look for releases every hour.
Update with a command: one paste for PowerShell or Terminal, in Settings, the README, the guide and the product page.
Settings → Version & updates can Restart, Repair files, make a Safety copy now and Stop Deja Vu1.
Starting a second launcher opens the copy that is already running.
Shorter About and update text.
Your phone connects by scanning a QR code, and the typed address shows its colon.
Help on every card, a nine-stop quick tour, and Demo printer 1, 2 and 3.
Install in one paste, clearer screenshots and share cards.

versions.name: Updates that find you
versions.summary: Deja Vu1 now updates itself, from newest builds, stable releases or git and GitHub Desktop copies, and shows which version you run. The 3D twin shows the real print in its colours, your settings keep safety copies, and a notification orb, an app window of its own and a tour of every screen arrive with it.

highlights.title: A version you can see
highlights.text: This number matches the release on GitHub. Every version below says what changed, and each one with a tour can walk you through it.

highlights.title: Updates for every kind of copy
highlights.text: A downloaded copy installs the published release. A copy made with git or GitHub Desktop pulls the newest version from GitHub, and stops if you edited its files by hand. Either way your settings and files stay put, and a failed start puts the old version back.

highlights.title: Newest builds or stable releases
highlights.text: Get each improvement as soon as it is published (only the changed files, each checked against GitHub's record), or only published releases. Updates can also install by themselves while every printer is idle.

highlights.title: The notification orb
highlights.text: Messages rise out of this glass orb in the corner and sink back into it. Click it to read the last 30 and to see update news.

highlights.title: A window of its own
highlights.text: Install Deja Vu1 as an app, or have the launcher open it in its own window with no tabs or address bar. The browser tab still works.

highlights.title: A tour of every screen
highlights.text: Replay setup walks through the dashboard with something to try at most stops. (Since this version it has become a nine-stop quick tour, with a few more tips on each screen, and the demo printers are called Demo printer 1, 2 and 3.)

highlights.title: The real print in the twin
highlights.text: The twin reads the file being printed and grows each layer's outside walls in the colour loaded in the head printing it. Take the case off to see the frame, motors and belts.

highlights.title: Insights from your history
highlights.text: Patterns from the printer's own history: what tends to fail, which files print well, and where time goes.

highlights.title: Your data is safe
highlights.text: Safety copies of your settings every six hours, at start-up and before every update, each restorable with an undo.

changes: Version history in Settings, matched to the VERSION file and to the GitHub release notes, with a full-screen interactive tour for each version.
In-app updates for git and GitHub Desktop copies: fast-forward only, refused when files were changed by hand, and rolled back if the new version fails its startup check.
Releases now publish by themselves: raising the VERSION number on main builds the update package and the GitHub release.
Automatic update checks, when you turn them on, now repeat daily while the server keeps running, not only at startup.
A translucent notification orb in the bottom-right corner replaces the messages at the top of the screen, with a history of the last 30.
Desktop app: install it from Chrome or Edge, or let the launcher open it in its own app window. Settings → Desktop app.
The setup tour now covers every screen with things to try, and explains the demo printers and the Photo studio tab.
The README and product page now open with the ways you can use Deja Vu1 and how the pieces connect.

Updates: a Newest builds channel that fetches only changed files, each checked against GitHub's record; automatic checks every 15 minutes and optional automatic install while every printer is idle; Update with git for git copies started without the launcher.
Digital twin: the print itself in its loaded colours, Case on / See-through / Case off, and a full engineering drawing sheet. The demo's Workshop printer prints two two-colour Benchies.
3D viewer: a textured 276 × 293 mm plate, a studio backdrop and better lighting. Mixed layer heights rebuilt around one question: what you want from the print.

Safety copies of the dashboard's memory every six hours, at start-up and before updates, with self-repairing records; insights from the printer's history; Orca import of recent projects and presets; an optional device lock; About, credits and Check it yourself.

versions.name: The real Benchy and a working online demo
versions.summary: Real sample models, mixed layer heights you can plan, 106 slicer settings, a farm desk, a logbook and an online demo you can click around in.

highlights.title: The real 3DBenchy
highlights.text: Add sample files gives the real 3DBenchy, a 24-tooth gear and a twisted vase, with G-code cut from them layer by layer.

highlights.title: The Layer stack
highlights.text: Plan mixed layer heights: a base layer, times N for each head, with the reasons a choice is crossed out.

highlights.title: The project converter
highlights.text: Turn a Bambu Studio or MakerWorld project into one the U1 can print, with a report of every change.

highlights.title: A logbook per printer
highlights.text: Problems, fixes and print hours for each printer. Failed prints are logged by themselves.

highlights.title: Search everything
highlights.text: Type here, or press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac), to jump to any screen, setting, printer or file.

changes: Sample files: the real 3DBenchy (public domain), a gear and a twisted vase replace the cubes and the L-bracket.
The Layer stack for mixed layer heights, with four smart set-ups.
106 OrcaSlicer process settings in a tabbed editor.
Farm desk, telemetry panel and a logbook for each printer.
The converter moved to the top of Files; a finder searches the whole dashboard.
The online demo simulates print controls, temperatures, queueing, the logbook and the converter.

versions.name: A realistic 3D twin and a livelier background
versions.summary: The digital twin became a detailed 3D model of the U1, and the background started reacting to your cursor.

highlights.title: The 3D twin
highlights.text: A detailed model of the U1 with live heads, bed, docks and spools. Drag to turn it; click a part for its details.

highlights.title: Model or drawing
highlights.text: Switch between the realistic model and an engineering drawing made from the same geometry.

highlights.title: A background that reacts
highlights.text: Dots, Constellation, Flow or Layer lines, in six colour sets. Try clicking the background, or triple-click it.

changes: Digital twin rebuilt in WebGL 2 with studio lighting, reflections and soft shadows; the drawing mode uses the same geometry.
Background: Dots by default, stronger reactions, Constellation style, Time of day colours and little surprises.
Launch videos version 14 and 15.

versions.name: Interface refresh
versions.summary: A new background, rewritten games, a full-screen setup and one sentence under the tab bar saying what each screen is for.

highlights.title: What each screen is for
highlights.text: This line changes with the tab and says what the screen does in one sentence.

highlights.title: Games while you wait
highlights.text: Pac-Man, Tetris, Snake and Sky Dash were rewritten to run smoothly at any screen refresh rate.

changes: Cursor-reactive background with Flow, Layer lines, Dots and Still.
First 3D twin beside the engineering drawing.
Pac-Man, Tetris, Snake and Sky Dash rewritten.
Full-screen setup with a Make it yours step; clearer tab names and introductions.

versions.name: Slicing workspace and app-data recovery
versions.summary: One workspace for objects, profiles and tools, real slices with separate layer heights per head, and a full backup you can restore.

highlights.title: Auto-print and slicing
highlights.text: Pick a profile and your fitted tools, slice with an installed engine, and queue the result after a pre-flight check.

highlights.title: A full backup
highlights.text: Download all your settings, files and printer records as one ZIP. Restoring checks it first and never replaces your running data.

changes: Unified slicing workspace: objects, profiles, fitted tools, status and preview.
Separate physical-head layer heights for capable engines.
3MF plates separated with recovery data.
Full app-data backup with checksums and isolated recovery.

versions.name: Plate editing, real slicing and a first updater
versions.summary: A plate editor, a real OrcaSlicer slice through the bridge, colour tiles from photos, camera snapshots and the first update checker.

highlights.title: Setup and help
highlights.text: A skippable setup you can replay any time. Your name, if you give one, stays in this browser.

highlights.title: Photo studio
highlights.text: Turn a photo into a colour-layered relief or tile using your four filament colours.

highlights.title: Camera snapshots
highlights.text: Pictures from the selected printer's own camera.

changes: Undoable multi-model plate editor and 3MF save-as.
Installed-preset discovery and a verified real OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 slice on Linux.
Four-tool image tiles, swatch sheets and heightmap reliefs.
Stock camera snapshots and time-lapse from each printer's camera.
Setup, feature search and the first opt-in update checker.

versions.name: Online demo, planner and printer finder

highlights.title: Find printers
highlights.text: Looks for U1 printers on your home network and tests the connection before adding one.

highlights.title: Skip one object
highlights.text: When a print labels its objects, pick one on the bed map and stop only that one.

changes: Online demo on the public page.
Digital twin version 2, drawn the drafting way.
Mixed-nozzle planner and a nozzle check in Confirm Print.
Find printers on the network; double-click starters for Windows, Mac and Linux.
Skip one object, multi-plate conversion fixes, Spoolman import, Add to Home Screen.

versions.name: The first dashboard
versions.summary: The start: a real Moonraker connection, the fleet, live updates, controls, Photo-to-Print Studio and the maintenance module it began with.

highlights.title: Your printers
highlights.text: One card per printer: state, progress, heads and health.

highlights.title: Honest controls
highlights.text: Pause, resume and cancel. A button shows what the printer reports back, never what it hoped for.

highlights.title: Care
highlights.text: Maintenance reminders counted from real print hours.

changes: Moonraker client written from Moonraker, Klipper and Snapmaker's U1 source.
Fleet command center, Photo-to-Print Studio, auto-print and the farm sandbox.
Live updates over WebSocket, files, G-code and 3D viewers, automations, phone layout.
Liquid Glass interface, games, printer control, pairing, notifications, filament tracking, maintenance.
